question: Say the restaurant's about two miles from me, what's your delivery charge going to be?
expected_answer: It's £1.99, the fee for 1 to 2.5 miles under the fee schedule in force since 3 August 2026.

meta.note: Superseded March 2025 schedule charged £2.49 for 1.5 to 3 miles; retrieval must pick the current one.

question: Is the service fee, like, a percent of the order on top of the delivery charge?
expected_answer: It's a percentage: the service fee is charged on top of the delivery fee at 9 percent of the basket subtotal, minimum £0.59, capped at £3.49 per order.

meta.note: Generic answer (yes, a small percentage-based service fee) is plausible but lacks the 9 percent rate, minimum and cap.

question: How much do we each pay if we split the delivery fee of three pounds four ways?
expected_answer: 75p each, because £3 divided by 4 is £0.75.

question: What's the smallest basket, um, in pounds, I can order on the quick grocery delivery?
expected_answer: Quick grocery orders need a minimum basket of £15, and the checkout won't go through below that.

meta.note: Scheduled grocery minimum is £40 and click-and-collect is £5 in the same doc (distractors).

question: Is there VAT on grocery basics like bread and milk, or is it the full twenty percent?
expected_answer: Most basic food like bread and milk is zero-rated for VAT in the UK; the 20 percent standard rate applies to things like crisps, sweets, alcohol and hot takeaway food.

question: If I end my membership today, will I keep my perks till the month's up?
expected_answer: No. Cancellation takes effect immediately, so member benefits stop the moment you cancel, and monthly members get no refund for the unused part of the month.

key_facts: benefits stop at the moment you cancel
no refund for the unused part of the month
core_facts: benefits stop at the moment you cancel
meta.note: Common norm: subscription benefits continue until the end of the period already paid for.

question: Um, what's the difference in price between paying for it monthly and yearly?
expected_answer: Membership is £7.99 a month, or £69 if you pay for a year.

history.content: Hi, I'm thinking about signing up for the membership thing on the app.
Happy to help with that. What would you like to know about it?

question: If your cancel button won't work, can my card provider stop the monthly payments for me?
expected_answer: Yes. Contact your card issuer and ask them to cancel the recurring payment (a continuous payment authority); they must stop it when you ask, though you still owe anything already due under the contract.

question: Can I still change the delivery address now, like after I've already placed the order?
expected_answer: Yes, in the app, but only before the rider collects the order and only to an address within 1 mile of the original; any higher distance band difference is charged.

key_facts: before the rider collects the order
core_facts: before the rider collects the order
meta.note: Generic answer is 'maybe, contact support'; the precise window and 1-mile limit are org specific.

question: Oh okay, but if I back out at this point, what do I still have to pay?
expected_answer: Because the restaurant has accepted it, cancelling now is charged at 50 percent of the food subtotal.

history.content: I ordered a pizza about five minutes ago and I've changed my mind.
No problem, let me take a look. It shows the restaurant has already accepted the order.

question: If I put the wrong flat number on my order, can I still message the rider?
expected_answer: Yes, message or call the rider straight away through the in-app chat or call option, and update the delivery note with the right flat number.

question: If something's missing from my order, do you put the refund back on my card, yeah?
expected_answer: Not by default. Approved refunds are paid as account credit unless you choose Refund to card when reporting, or ask within 7 days while the credit is unused; card refunds take 3 to 5 working days.

key_facts: approved refunds are paid as Brambleway credit
core_facts: approved refunds are paid as Brambleway credit
meta.note: Common norm: refunds go back to the original payment method.

question: How soon should I report a missing item on a grocery order, is it within a day?
expected_answer: For grocery orders you have 72 hours from delivery; the 24-hour limit only applies to restaurant orders.

meta.note: Generic answer ('as soon as possible, usually within 24 to 48 hours') is plausible but wrong for grocery; restaurant limit is 24 hours.

question: If I want a refund for a damaged item, should I take a photo of it first?
expected_answer: Yes, photograph the item and its packaging (and the label or receipt) before you throw anything away, so you have evidence for the claim.

key_facts: photo of the item and packaging
core_facts: photo of the item and packaging

question: If I've no ID for the beer in my grocery order, will they still hand over the rest?
expected_answer: No. On grocery orders the whole order is returned to the hub because sealed bags can't be split at the door, and you're refunded minus a £5 failed ID check fee.

meta.note: Common norm: only the age-restricted items are removed and the rest is handed over (true here only for restaurant orders).

question: Up in Glasgow, will I still be able to order wine at like half ten at night?
expected_answer: No. In Scotland alcohol orders are only accepted until 9:30 pm, so that delivery is completed by 10 pm.

meta.note: England and Wales cutoff is 11 pm in the same doc; Glasgow quick grocery hours run to 11 pm (distractor).

question: Is the legal age for buying wine in Glasgow eighteen, same as down in England, right?
expected_answer: Yes, the legal age to buy alcohol is 18 everywhere in the UK, including Scotland.

question: Can I just hand a swap back to the rider at the door if I don't want it?
expected_answer: No, substitutes can't be handed back to the rider; reject it in the app within 2 hours of delivery and you get credit for the full substitute price.

key_facts: can't be handed back to the rider
core_facts: can't be handed back to the rider
meta.note: Common norm for grocery delivery: unwanted substitutes can be refused and handed back at the door.

question: They swapped my semi skimmed for whole milk, so how much more fat is in it?
expected_answer: Yes, whole milk is about 3.5% fat and semi-skimmed is about 1.7%, so whole milk has roughly twice the fat.

history.content: Hi, my grocery order came with a couple of swaps in it.
Sorry about that. Which item was substituted?

question: On a Saturday night in Leeds, until when do you keep bringing restaurant food round?
expected_answer: Restaurant delivery in Leeds runs until 2 am on Friday and Saturday nights.

meta.note: Quick grocery doc says Leeds runs to midnight (near-duplicate distractor).

question: Um, on a weekday in Bristol, when does your quick grocery delivery stop for the night?
expected_answer: In Bristol quick grocery runs from 8 am to 10 pm Sunday to Thursday, and until 11 pm on Friday and Saturday.

meta.note: Restaurant doc says 11 pm on weekdays and midnight at weekends for Bristol (near-duplicate distractor).

question: If I order late on a Saturday night, how long do you reckon leftovers keep?
expected_answer: Eat refrigerated leftovers within 2 days, and cooked rice within 24 hours; cool them and get them in the fridge within a couple of hours.

question: I forgot to tip at checkout, but can I still add one, and for how long?
expected_answer: You can add a tip from the order page for up to 48 hours after the order is delivered.

key_facts: up to 48 hours after the order is delivered
core_facts: up to 48 hours after the order is delivered

question: If nobody hears the buzzer, how long will the rider hang around before they leave?
expected_answer: The rider waits 8 minutes and tries to call you twice; after that the order is returned, marked as delivered and not refunded, unless you chose Leave at door.

question: How long will a hot takeaway, um, be okay sitting on the doorstep for?
expected_answer: Hot food shouldn't be left out at room temperature for more than about 2 hours; after that it's safest to throw it away.

question: How much do I need to spend for the new customer discount code to actually work?
expected_answer: The £8 welcome code needs a minimum spend of £20 on food, not counting fees or tips, used within 14 days of creating the account.

question: So if I forget to cancel it, will it just start charging me automatically after?
expected_answer: No. The trial does not roll into a paid membership automatically; benefits stop after 30 days and you're only charged if you choose to continue by tapping Keep Plus.

history.content: I just saw there's a free trial for the membership.
That's right, new members can try it free for thirty days.

key_facts: does not roll into a paid membership automatically
core_facts: does not roll into a paid membership automatically
meta.note: Common norm: free trials convert to a paid subscription automatically unless cancelled.

question: If I get fifteen percent off a twenty four pound order with you, what does that save me?
expected_answer: You save £3.60, so you'd pay £20.40.

question: If I'm running a bit late for my click and collect, they'll just hold it for me, yeah?
expected_answer: Only briefly: restaurant orders are held for 15 minutes after the ready time (grocery hubs 30), then cancelled and charged in full with no refund; you can add 10 minutes once with I'm running late.

key_facts: held for 15 minutes after the ready time
charged in full with no refund
core_facts: held for 15 minutes after the ready time
meta.note: Common norm: shops hold click-and-collect orders for a generous period, often days.

question: Yeah, for the chilled stuff I've just collected from you, how cold does my fridge actually need to be?
expected_answer: Keep your fridge at 5°C or below, ideally between 0 and 5°C.

history.content: I've just picked up my shopping from the collection point.
Great, glad that went smoothly. Is there anything else I can help with?
